paper.title_en: Time Travel Paradoxes and Entangled Timelines
paper.abstract_en: For time travel to be consistent with the known laws of physics, the resulting paradoxes must be resolved. It has been suggested that the notion of parallel timelines may provide a resolution, by allowing different events to happen in different timelines. However, so far, a concrete mechanism by which parallel timelines can be created has never been satisfactorily formulated in a way that makes the relationships between the timelines clear. In this paper, we propose such a mechanism based on the Everett (many-worlds) interpretation of quantum mechanics. The timelines in our model are variants of the "worlds" of the Everett interpretation that can connect to each other via the time machine. They are created by the entanglement of the time machine with the environment and the resulting decoherence; therefore, we call them "entangled timelines" or E-CTCs. As the entanglement gradually spreads out to additional systems, the timelines spread out as well, providing a local and well-defined mechanism for branching timelines. The E-CTC model is similar to Deutsch's familiar D-CTC model but differs from it mainly by imposing a different consistency condition, based on pure states, which allows the information about the entanglement to be preserved. These differences allow us to create a clearer practical definition of the timelines and avoid some of the surprising consequences of the D-CTC model's non-linear evolution.
